chunks: Muḥammad ibn Qays narrated from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام that he said:
Regarding a man who had four wives and divorced one of them, then married another woman before the divorced woman had completed her waiting period, he ruled:

That the latter wife should return to her family until the divorced woman completes her term, and then the other woman is to begin another waiting period. She is entitled to her dowry if he had consummated the marriage with her; but if he had not consummated the marriage with her, then she has no dowry and no waiting period from him.
Then, if her family wish after the completion of her waiting period, they may marry her to him, and if they wish, they may refuse.

key_terms.أَرْبَعُ نِسْوَةٍ: four wives, the maximum number relevant to the ruling
key_terms.أَهْلُهَا: her family, who may later marry her to him again
key_terms.الْأَخِيرَةُ: the latter woman whom he married afterward
key_terms.دَخَلَ بِهَا: he consummated the marriage with her
key_terms.فَطَلَّقَ: he divorced, initiating the legal waiting period

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a man marries a fifth wife before his divorced wife's waiting period ends?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on a man who already had four wives, divorced one, and then married another before the first wife's 'iddah ended. The ruling requires separation from the latter wife until the first wife's waiting period ends, and it clarifies the consequences regarding a new waiting period and dowry depending on whether consummation took place.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.4461 - Muhammad ibn Qays narrated from Abu Ja'far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as):
Regarding a man who had four wives and divorced one of them, then married another woman before the divorced wife had completed her waiting period.

Imam (as) ruled: "The latter wife must return to her family until the divorced wife completes her waiting period. After that, the latter wife must observe a new waiting period. If he had consummated the marriage with her, she is entitled to her dowry. However, if he had not consummated the marriage, she has no dowry and no waiting period required for her.
After her waiting period ends, if her family wishes, they may give her back in marriage to him, and if they wish, they may refuse."
